methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements that capture a single aspect of the design or functionality.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module interface defined with clk, d, reset, and q
d is an 8-bit data input
reset is an active-high synchronous reset signal
q is an 8-bit output register
Combinational logic generates D input based on reset and d
If reset is asserted, D input is set to reset_value (0x34)
If reset is not asserted, D input is set to d
D[i] = (reset) ? reset_value[i] : d[i]
reset_value = 8'b00110100
Combinational logic can be viewed as eight 2-to-1 multiplexers
D[i] = (reset & reset_value[i]) | (!reset & d[i])
q updates on the negative edge of clk
When reset is high, q is synchronously reset to 0x34 on the next negative edge of clk
When reset is low, q takes the value of d on the next negative edge of clk
d must be stable before the negative edge of clk
reset must be stable before the negative edge of clk
Flip-flops are negative edge-triggered
reset is synchronous and active high
register is initialized to 0x34 when reset is asserted
Update of q is implemented using non-blocking assignments within an always @(negedge clk) block
